## Command Details

```text
Register External Effect contracts, propose exact requests,
authorize them drift-bound, settle governed executions, and
compensate committed effects (F056 T1-T4).
Amber forbids arbitrary account-bearing external operations: the
only thing that can ever execute externally is a registered effect
contract. Each contract declares the external owner, one system
type (ticketing|code-review|notification|deployment|storage), one
registered operation name, the exact external target and scope,
idempotency behavior (idempotent|at-most-once), a credentials class
(none|scoped), the receipt fields the external system must return,
a compensation declaration — a named compensating effect or an
explicit irreversibility marker — a bounded timeout (at most 24h),
and the one registered F051 Adapter pin (id + version, verified at
registration) that owns the API. Registration settles behind a
single-use committed human Decision (acceptance|approval with a
verified principal snapshot) into a hash-chained append-only ledger
under .amber/external/ and is immutable per effect id@version —
changed external semantics register a new version, and stale pins
refuse downstream. No contract field can carry a command,
executable, or remote URL: every external-facing name is a closed
slug (no whitespace, no URL scheme, no shell metacharacters, no ".."
traversal segments), so free-form execution vectors refuse by
construction. `effects` is a read-only projection of the registry
and fails closed on a corrupt ledger.
`propose` is a governance-write that binds one registered effect
version (its current head), the contract's exact target and scope,
the canonical payload hash, the credentials class, and the declared
compensation into a canonical requestHash — review binds exactly
what will happen. Idempotency binds owner + effect + target +
scope + payloadHash: an identical request refuses naming the
existing proposal, so a retry can never create a duplicate external
record. `authorize` consumes one single-use Approval whose subject
binds external-effect:<requestHash> and settles the human Decision
atomically with the consumption; effect-version or Adapter-version
drift since the proposal refuses — a stale authorization can never
ride changed external semantics. `proposals` lists the requests
read-only.
`execute` prepares one execution for an AUTHORIZED request: the
operation, target, scope, and Adapter pin come only from the
reviewed contract snapshot (caller input can never supply a
command, executable, or URL; the request re-derives one last time
so post-authorization drift refuses), and a scoped-credentials
contract binds a short-lived purpose/scope/expiry credential
boundary whose expiry is bounded by the contract timeout — no
handle or value field exists in any stored shape, and
credential-looking material refuses with
AMBER_E_EXTERNAL_CREDENTIAL_LEAK. One execution is open per
request; a committed request never re-executes, and an unconfirmed
(attempted|unknown) outcome retries only under a contract declared
idempotent. `settle` records the Adapter's declared result receipt
(real external record id, request/response digests, declared
status) and Amber — never the adapter — derives the terminal
outcome (denied|attempted|committed|failed|unknown): committed
requires the record id AND response digest (missing output reads
as its refusal, never success), a claimed failure without the
response digest downgrades to attempted, and settled outcomes
never re-settle. `reconcile` is the only path from unknown to
committed: it requires recorded reconciliation Evidence from a
producer independent of the authorizing approver. `status` reads
one execution with its settlement and reconciliation.
`compensate` opens a NEW governed proposal for one committed (or
failed-partial) execution: it rides exactly the compensation the
ORIGINAL contract declared (an irreversible contract refuses), it
records the original execution id as its compensates linkage, one
compensation lineage exists per original, and it then goes through
its own authorization, execution, and receipt — the original
outcome is never rewritten. `transactions` is the read-time
projection joining every execution with its compensation lineage;
`compensated` flips only when a compensating execution actually
committed. Nothing under this command executes an external
operation, MCP surfaces only the approval-required proposal
contract and never spawns it, and the ADR-0020 sync
transport exception stays untouched.

  amber external transactions --target . --request request/ticket-comment-288 --json
```

## Boundaries & Safety

- `--target <path>` selects repository state. Amber confines these target-relative paths, refusing `..` and symlink escapes before reading or writing: plan and scaffold destinations (including `accept --plan`), memory and context payloads, harness inputs, adapter allow-lists, workflow reports and their output directory, ledger exports, execution readiness plans, session and worktree state, governance report output, wiki export and handoff bundle output directories.
- Path validation is not OS sandboxing, and the confinement above covers only the surfaces it names, and a confined flag still accepts an absolute destination only when it stays inside the target. `governance audit --output`, `governance readiness --output`, `security audit --output`, `loop record --output`, and `explain --markdown` resolve against the working directory instead of `--target`. A path flag not listed here is confined only when the command that reads it routes through the boundary. A governed or verification command still runs with your user's file permissions.
- `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, `workflow assess` and `governance report` reject output destinations that resolve to the target root, including `.`, an absolute root path, `nested/..`, and symlink or junction aliases of the root. Output subdirectories and defaults are unchanged.
- `wiki export` and `handoff bundle` check all planned file destinations and their parent directories before the first write, including copied wiki pages and optional replay files. An existing child symlink or junction outside the target refuses the export without changing output files. `wiki export` also checks every page it copies, so a page that shares its bytes with another name refuses the export before anything is written, including when both names stay inside the target. Concurrent link replacement is not prevented.
- A planned output file that shares its bytes with another name — a hard link, or a link to one — is refused before the write by `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, `workflow assess --output-dir`, `governance report --output`, `ledger export --out`, `knowledge context-review-sample --output`, `gate --plan` and `accept --plan` (the plan file they edit in place), `handoff` (the `session-handoff.md` it overwrites), `hooks install` (the `pre-commit` hook and its `.amber-backup` it overwrites), `knowledge plan propose` (the plan file it overwrites when `--force`) and `sync --execute` / scaffold refresh (the controlled template files it overwrites and their `.bak` copies) — and `amber context benchmark` applies the same refusal to the benchmark reports it persists — even when both names stay inside the target. A link to a single in-target file is still written through, so it replaces that file's bytes; `workflow assess` is the exception, because it confines its output file to the `--output-dir` and so refuses a link whose referent sits elsewhere in the target. Like the child-link check above, this is checked before the write, so a link swapped in during the write is not caught.
- `handoff validate --bundle-dir .` and `workflow assess --handoff-bundle-dir .` still accept root-level bundles as read-only inputs. Explicit handoff validation paths outside `--target` are refused.
- Writing governance state goes through two shared helpers — the in-place JSON writer and the append-only JSONL ledger append — and both refuse a leaf that shares its bytes with another name. That covers the `.amber/` writers built on them (context pages and Loadouts, audit and event ledgers) without each one repeating the check; a raw write outside those helpers is guarded only where its own surface names it above.
- **Fail-Closed Behavior**: Corrupt governance state or invalid schema parameters immediately halt execution with non-zero exit codes.
